subtopic: Token Holder Rights vs. Underlying Shareholder Rights
source_evidence: The rights, obligations and benefits received by the token holder of a synthetic tokenized security may differ significantly from those of a traditional owner in the underlying security.
question: Misconception: Anyone who holds a tokenized security automatically has the same rights as a shareholder who owns the underlying shares directly.
answer: Correction: Rights depend on the tokenization model. Issuer-sponsored tokens carry the same legal rights as a traditional share of the same class, and custodial tokens represent an indirect interest with the same rights, obligations, and benefits as a traditional shareholder. But synthetic tokens may provide different rights, and their holders have no claims or rights against the issuer of the referenced security.
